Thesis Shift: Headline Miss vs Microcap Baseline

Consensus called for $0.57M in Q3 revenue. AEye delivered $0.51M (~10x YoY and 2.5x QoQ) falling -$0.06M (-10.53%) shy of consensus due to delivery timing on prototype contracts. However, customer accounts expanded to 32.

Forward Expectations: Doubling to $1M Q4 Baseline

Management initiated Q4 revenue guidance of approximately double Q3 to ~$1.00M, marking AEye's first million-dollar quarter and establishing a new quarterly revenue baseline supported by binding Lunar Outpost milestones and repeat defense purchasing.

Balance Sheet De-Risking: Cash Extends to 2028

AEye tapped its ATM facility to boost cash & marketable securities to $63.1M. With full-year 2026 cash consumption guided at $35M and targeting a ~15% cut in 2027 burn, liquidity is locked into 2028.

Forensic Cash Quality & Balance Sheet Fortress Assessment

AEye recorded disciplined cash management in Q3 2026 with Operating Cash Flow of $-8.05M and Reported Free Cash Flow of $-8.06M. Non-cash stock-based compensation totaled $3.25M, leading to Forensic True Free Cash Flow of $-11.31M.

• Capital Efficiency: CapEx remained negligible at $0.01M in Q3 2026 ($0.33M YTD), demonstrating AEye's pure software-defined, asset-light operating model. Tier-1 partners manage physical fabrication.
• Balance Sheet Infusion: Cash and marketable securities rose from $32.50M in Q2 to $63.10M as of September 30, 2026, benefiting from disciplined ATM equity sales that secured growth capital without institutional debt covenants.
• Cash Runway Horizon: With 2026 cash consumption guided at $35.0M ($8.3M in Q3) and management targeting a ~15% reduction in 2027 burn (~$29.8M), the existing $63.1M treasury extends liquidity runway comfortably into 2028.
Row 4: Operational Wins, Drags & Earnings Call Q&A Audit
QUALITATIVE & TRANSCRIPT FORENSICS

Operational Wins & Catalysts

  • Lunar Outpost Binding Contract: Initiated revenue recognition under multi-million-dollar binding agreement, supplying Apollo™ for the Pegasus Lunar Terrain Vehicle from qualification through flight delivery.
  • Fifth Repeat Defense Order: Lead defense customer placed its 5th repeat purchase order, confirming expanding defense adoption for counter-UAS and tactical situational awareness.
  • Rapid Customer Expansion: Commercial revenue-generating customers climbed to 32 (up 28% QoQ from 25), with over 200 qualified technical engagements in the active sales pipeline.
  • Massive Margin Rebound: Gross margin improved from -80% in Q2 to -33% in Q3 (+47 percentage points) due to Apollo BOM cost reductions and STRATOS contribution.

Execution Drags & Watch Items

  • Headline Revenue Miss: Q3 revenue of $0.51M fell short of $0.57M consensus due to milestone recognition timing slipping into early Q4.
  • Sub-$1.00 NASDAQ Minimum Bid: Stock trades at $0.89 close / $0.87 after hours, maintaining compliance pressure under NASDAQ listing rules.
  • Ongoing Operating Cash Burn: Quarterly operating cash burn remained elevated at -$8.05M (-$23.89M YTD), requiring strict adherence to the $35M annual budget.
  • Microcap Liquidity Horizon: Limited daily share trading turnover restricts large institutional allocators pending commercial production scale.
Top Institutional Analyst Q&A and Analyst Questions Forensic Exchanges
Kevin Garrigan (WestPark Capital) — Q4 2026 $1M Revenue Target & Lunar Outpost Commercial Ramp

Question: Can you discuss what provides the confidence to guide Q4 revenue doubling to ~$1.0 million, and how much of that is driven by recurring hardware shipments versus Lunar Outpost development milestones?

Executive Answer: Matt Fisch (CEO): 'Our visibility into Q4 comes from binding purchase orders and committed program schedules. Lunar Outpost is now contributing under our multi-million-dollar contract as Apollo moves from qualification into flight hardware fabrication. Simultaneously, our lead defense customer placed its fifth order, and repeat commercial orders across our 32 active accounts provide the foundation for this $1M quarterly baseline.'

Forensic Assessment: CLEAR VISIBILITY TO $1M BASELINE
Casey Ryan (WestPark Capital) — Gross Margin Progression & STRATOS Counter-UAS Unit Economics

Question: Gross margin improved substantially from -80% in Q2 to -33% in Q3. How does the STRATOS revenue mix with Swiftstrike AI impact margin progression into positive territory in 2027?

Executive Answer: Conor Tierney (CFO): 'The 47-percentage-point sequential gross margin improvement reflects three factors: lower bill-of-materials costs as Apollo reaches volume, lower warranty accruals, and an initial contribution from STRATOS. Because STRATOS incorporates our software-defined architecture, it commands higher software attachment rates and better ASPs. As commercial volumes ramp through 2027, we expect to cross into positive gross margins.'

Forensic Assessment: GROSS MARGIN INFLECTION CONFIRMED
Institutional Tech Specialist — ATM Utilization, Balance Sheet Cash, and Runway into 2028

Question: Ending cash rose to $63.1 million this quarter. Can you detail the capital raised under your ATM facility, your planned cash burn for 2027, and whether additional equity financing is needed?

Executive Answer: Conor Tierney (CFO): 'We strategically tapped our ATM facility during periods of liquidity to build a fortress balance sheet with $63.1M in cash and marketable securities and virtually zero debt. With full-year 2026 cash consumption guided at $35M and our commitment to reduce burn by ~15% in 2027, our cash runway now comfortably extends into 2028 without requiring near-term capital raises.'

Forensic Assessment: RUNWAY EXTENDED TO 2028

Desk Takeaway & Driver: AEye shares dipped -2.25% to $0.87 in after-hours trading as Q3 revenue ($0.51M) came in below Street consensus ($0.57M). However, the downside was cushioned by management's strong forward guidance of approximately doubling Q4 revenue to ~$1.00M, gross margin improvement from -80% to -33%, customer accounts growing to 32, and cash surging to $63.1M extending operating runway into 2028.
